steps.say: Scientists ask a question. Then they predict what will happen.
In a fair test, change one thing. Keep everything else the same.
Measure carefully. Use a ruler for length and a thermometer for temperature.
Record your results in a table. Then you can compare them.

head: Ball
Bounce height
figure.alt: Table: rubber ball bounced 70 cm, football bounced 45 cm.

steps.say: A bar chart shows results as bars. The tallest bar shows the biggest result.

figure.alt: Bar chart: rubber ball 70 cm, football 45 cm.

steps.say: Say what you found out, even if your prediction was wrong.

check.prompt: In a fair test, how many things do you change?

options.why: With two changes, you cannot tell which one made the difference.
If you change everything, you cannot tell what made the difference.
If nothing changes, there is nothing to test.

hints: A fair test finds out what made a difference.
If two things change, which one caused it?
Ask: how many things can you test at once?
check.explanation: In a fair test you change one thing and keep everything else the same.
